title: Multipath session aggregation and finalization for fragmented/partial streaming requests
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We currently mis-credit or leave unfinalized token usage when a client opens multi-path streaming sessions (eg client-side fanout, multiplexed HTTP/2 streams, or worker-level substreams) that later merge or drop midflight. This causes two recurring issues: (1) provisional token counts are either double-counted when fragments rehydrate on resume, or lost when the connection aborts without a terminal marker; (2) quota and rate limiter interactions are noisy because provisional credits are immediately applied to quota windows.

Goal: Implement a deterministic session aggregation and finalization protocol in the metering pipeline that ensures: (a) every fragment is accounted exactly-once; (b) provisional accounting is reversible until finalization; (c) rate limits and quotas reflect final committed usage for enforcement but can surface provisional usage for UX/visibility without affecting hard limits.

Scope: streaming generation (WS/HTTP2), multiplexed client behaviors, cross-worker fragment reassembly, reconnect/resume scenarios, and billing telemetry ingestion/consumption. This ticket focuses on the server-side metering ledger and the finalization contract; separate follow-ups will update SDK examples and Console UX.
background: Recent incidents: customer-reported spikes where short-lived mobile reconnections led to 2x billing for some sessions (postmortem linked below). Current ledger model treats any received chunk as immediately committed which breaks when fragments are replayed or re-sent. Existing partial-retry mitigation heuristics (ENG-314159, ENG-74021) reduce noise but do not guarantee deterministic finalization across multi-path fanout or worker handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Implement session-level finalization with a configurable finalization window and watermark-based commit semantics
Ensure ledger shows provisional -> committed transitions with audit trail visible in Console for sample sessions
No customer-visible double-billing in canary region over 7 days of synthetic reconnection/retry tests
Rate limiter must not permanently deduct quota for provisional credits; enforcement should only apply on committed counts
Reconciliation job to ingest late fragments and retroactively commit/correct ledger within SLA (<= 5 minutes for typical cases)
Comprehensive unit/integration tests and chaos tests for out-of-order fragments, duplicate fragments, and midstream aborts
design_notes:
Proposal summary:

1) Session ID canonicalization: require a top-level session id generated by the fronting gateway or assigned by runtime on first fragment. All fragments for the logical request must include session_id and fragment_seq (monotonic per session). For legacy clients without session_id, runtime will synthesize a stable session id using connection + nonce and mark it 'synthesized'.

2) Provisional ledger entries: when a fragment (partial token delta) arrives, write a provisional ledger row: {session_id, fragment_seq, token_delta, checksum, provisional:true, received_ts}. Provisional rows do not affect committed quota counters.

3) Finalization contract: clients (SDK or runtime) send an explicit 'session_end' marker with final sequence and total checksum. If session_end arrives, reconcile the fragments for session, validate checksum, and atomically mark provisional rows as committed; then increment committed quota counters and emit billing events.

4) Watermark & auto-finalize: to handle clients that do not send session_end (network drop), introduce a configurable finalization_window (default 60s) per session. After watermark (last_fragment_ts + finalization_window) the backend runs an auto-finalize pass which validates sequence continuity and marks the session committed. Auto-finalize only commits continuous sequences; otherwise it schedules a reconciliation attempt.

5) Duplicate/dedup handling: use fragment checksum and fragment_seq to deduplicate; if a fragment with same seq but different checksum appears, flag for manual review and route to reconciliation pipeline.

6) Late fragments and retroactive corrections: a reconciliation consumer replays late fragments into an append-only correction log. Corrections are applied as adjustments (positive/negative) to the ledger with explicit audit metadata and do not trigger immediate enforcement changes until corrections are committed.

7) Quota/rate limiter interaction: enforcement uses 'committed' counts. To prevent soft-denial surprises, the Console shows provisional usage in near-real-time but enforcement for quota blocks uses the last committed snapshot plus a configurable safety buffer. We will default buffer to 5% during rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement server-side ledger + provisional APIs behind feature flag 'multipath-metering'. 2) Canary rollout to 'us-west-2-canary' (10% of requests), shadow enforcement enabled: ledger commits but does not deduct quota; differences logged. 3) Run synthetic test harness for 7 days simulating mobile reconnections, HTTP/2 stream merging, and worker handoffs. 4) If diffs <= 0.1% (no double-billing) and no missed commits >= 1% of sessions, enable full enforcement in canary. 5) Gradual ramp to remaining regions in 3 waves. 6) After 30 days of production stability, remove safety buffer and GA the feature.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for ledger write/dedup/commit transitions.
- Integration test: local proxy simulating multiplexed client opening two substreams that merge into one session; assert final committed token equals canonical model run.
- Chaos tests: drop middle fragments, replay duplicates, swap fragment order.
- Synthetic billing sim: 10k sessions/day in canary ramp, compare committed charges vs current algorithm.
- End-to-end smoke with rate limiter: attempt to hit quota at boundary while provisional credits present; ensure enforcement only triggers based on committed snapshot and buffer.
- Backfill reconciliation test: inject late fragment after commit and verify correction entries and negative adjustments are reflected in audit logs and Console with correct timestamps.
metrics: Primary: percent of sessions with corrected final token delta after reconciliation (target < 0.1%). Secondary: number of double-charge incidents in canary (target 0), average time-to-finalize (median < 45s), reconciliation lag (95th percentile < 5min).
monitoring: Dashboards: 'metering.finalization.latency', 'metering.provisional_vs_committed.delta', 'metering.duplicate_fragments.rate', 'billing.corrections.rate'. Alerts: threshold for corrections.rate > 0.5% triggers paging to SRE and product. Include a daily digest of committed vs provisional deltas for customer-facing accounts.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Mis-synthesized session IDs for legacy clients causing unintended aggregation across sessions. Mitigation: mark synthesized sessions in ledger and do not auto-finalize across connection restarts for synthesized ids; require explicit end or stronger heuristics.
Risk: Large numbers of provisional rows increase storage/ingest cost. Mitigation: compaction job to compact per-session fragments into a single provisional delta after N fragments or after 10s.
Risk: Reconciliation causing retroactive negative charges creating customer confusion. Mitigation: show correction events in Console, send customers an explanatory email for corrections above threshold, and provide API hooks for fetching audit records.
comments: 2026-02-16 | Ava Chen: Kicked off spike to enumerate client multiplexing patterns. Found three SDK behaviors (explicit session_id, connection-based sessions, and ad-hoc fanout from client). Sizing provisional row volume estimate ~ 12% increase during peak.

2026-02-22 | Diego Morales: Implemented provisional ledger schema and basic dedup by (session_id, fragment_seq). Pushed branch and opened PR. Need to add checksum validation and synth session guardrails.

2026-03-02 | SRE - Priya Nair: Load test notes: auto-finalize window of 60s increases meter write traffic but commit write amplification acceptable. Recommend default window 60s; expose as org-level runtime override for customers needing lower latency.

2026-03-05 | PM - Leo Fischer: Customer impact assessment ready. Large customers with mobile SDKs prefer shorter finalization for near-real-time billing. We'll add per-customer config behind enterprise flag.

2026-03-10 | Diego Morales: Canary feature-flag deployed to us-west-2-canary. Shadow commit enabled. Initial 24h run shows 0.04% sessions with post-commit corrections (good). Next: run full 7-day synthetic harness.
